snippet.title: Bukele, HÉROE NACIONAL en Haití: multitudes agradecen lucha contra temibles pandillas
snippet.description:
Verdadero héroe nacional para los haitianos, luego de haber desatado una implacable lucha contra la criminalidad que tenía asfixiado a su país, ahora Bukele está consolidando certeras acciones de sus fuerzas militares en busca de los cuatro aerotécnicos secuestrados por las pandillas en Puerto Príncipe y en cumplimiento de esa misión, los soldados salvadoreños han dado duros golpes a las bandas haitianas.

Esto ha provocado este estallido de celebraciones entre miles y miles de haitianos que salieron a bailar y cantar para agradecerle, el movimiento juvenil "relevo" ha sido el principal convocante y organizador de las movilizaciones masivas pro-bukele en Haití.

Además de asociaciones de víctimas de la violencia, ciudadanos afectados, desplazados y sobrevivientes de los delitos de las pandillas en las zonas más críticas de la capital, se han sumado líderes de comunidades religiosas y culturales.

Las marchas de agradecimiento y respaldo a Bukele han tenido un fuerte componente de identidad cultural, con ceremonias tradicionales y espirituales de los haitianos. El reconocimiento y gratitud de un pueblo agobiado por la violencia y apoyado por un presidente extranjero que ha hecho más por ellos que muchos de los gobernantes locales, a lo largo de años de azote de la violencia en Haití.

localized.title: Bukele, HÉROE NACIONAL en Haití: multitudes agradecen lucha contra temibles pandillas
localized.description:
Verdadero héroe nacional para los haitianos, luego de haber desatado una implacable lucha contra la criminalidad que tenía asfixiado a su país, ahora Bukele está consolidando certeras acciones de sus fuerzas militares en busca de los cuatro aerotécnicos secuestrados por las pandillas en Puerto Príncipe y en cumplimiento de esa misión, los soldados salvadoreños han dado duros golpes a las bandas haitianas.

Esto ha provocado este estallido de celebraciones entre miles y miles de haitianos que salieron a bailar y cantar para agradecerle, el movimiento juvenil "relevo" ha sido el principal convocante y organizador de las movilizaciones masivas pro-bukele en Haití.

Además de asociaciones de víctimas de la violencia, ciudadanos afectados, desplazados y sobrevivientes de los delitos de las pandillas en las zonas más críticas de la capital, se han sumado líderes de comunidades religiosas y culturales.

Las marchas de agradecimiento y respaldo a Bukele han tenido un fuerte componente de identidad cultural, con ceremonias tradicionales y espirituales de los haitianos. El reconocimiento y gratitud de un pueblo agobiado por la violencia y apoyado por un presidente extranjero que ha hecho más por ellos que muchos de los gobernantes locales, a lo largo de años de azote de la violencia en Haití.

At what point does incompetence become corruption? And how much longer does World Rugby expect rugby supporters to simply accept questionable officiating and pretend nothing happened?

France defeated South Africa 21–19 in Paris, but the controversy surrounding referee Andrea Piardi and TMO Matteo Liperini has raised questions that go far beyond one rugby match.

In Part 3 of my France vs South Africa refereeing analysis, we examine the lineout infringements, the controversial disallowed Kurt-Lee Arendse try, and what I believe was an astonishingly inconsistent performance from the television match official.

First, the lineouts.

Throughout the match, French players repeatedly appeared to jump across the lineout and interfere with South African jumpers. We also examine incidents where French defenders appeared to deliberately collapse Springbok lineout mauls.

Yet once again, Andrea Piardi's interpretation and application of the laws raises serious questions.

But the biggest controversy involves the TMO, Matteo Liperini.

How does a TMO suddenly develop an extraordinary eye for detail when South Africa scores, yet seemingly overlook serious infringements committed by France?

Kurt-Lee Arendse scored what appeared to be a brilliant Springbok try following a clever lineout move, with the ball thrown beyond the 15-metre line.

But Liperini intervened, identifying a marginal offside infringement that ultimately resulted in the try being disallowed.

Fine. If an infringement occurred and the laws and TMO protocols justify intervention, then apply them.

But here's the problem: Where was that same level of scrutiny for France?

Where was the intervention when Jan-Hendrik Wessels appeared to be obstructed during a French attacking movement that eventually resulted in a try?

Where was the intervention for the disputed deliberate knock-on just metres from France's try line, which potentially prevented a Springbok scoring opportunity?

And where was the consistency when French defenders repeatedly appeared to use illegal knee-drop tackles throughout the match?

Not every infringement falls within the TMO's intervention powers. But that makes understanding the protocols, identifying the available evidence and demanding consistent application even more important.

Why did the officiating appear so precise when examining South Africa, yet so much less convincing when France were the team under scrutiny?

And then there's World Rugby.

Following the match, Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus publicly questioned the TMO's failure to intervene and raised the possibility of match-fixing if infringements were knowingly ignored.

World Rugby's response?

A six-match suspension for Erasmus over his comments about the match officials.

Let that sink in.

The Springbok coach raises questions about officiating integrity and accountability, and he's the one facing disciplinary consequences.

But what about the decisions that prompted those questions in the first place?

Where is the transparency surrounding referee assessments? Where is the public accountability? And how can supporters have confidence in officiating standards when controversial performances continue to raise these questions?

Let me be clear: Poor officiating is not proof of corruption or match-fixing.

But neither should accusations of misconduct prevent legitimate scrutiny of refereeing decisions, TMO interventions and World Rugby's oversight of its officials.

In this video, I break down the footage, examine the relevant laws and question whether the decisions were applied consistently.

You don't have to agree with my conclusions.

But you should be able to watch the evidence and ask questions without being told to simply move on.

At what point does repeated incompetence become an issue of integrity and accountability?

Assistant Referee 1: Christophe Ridley (RFU)  
Assistant Referee 2: Gianluca Gnecchi (FIR)  
TMO: Matteo Liperini (FIR)

snippet.title: Ukraine Isn't Finished—Zelenskyy Warns Russia More Is Coming

I examine the reported collapse of a Kerch Bridge road span into the Kerch Strait and the message Kyiv attached to it: President Zelenskyy and Defense Minister Kamara both signaled that further Ukrainian operations could follow. I discuss the reported use of Ukrainian-made systems—including missile drones, Neptune missiles, Ruta, and FP-5 Flamingo weapons—and why the bridge remains a critical Russian military artery connecting occupied Crimea.

I also assess the larger strategic picture: Britain’s pledged short-range air-defense missiles and radars, Swedish aid for air defense and long-range strike capability, joint Ukrainian-Finnish production, German testing of Ukraine’s Delta combat-management system, and additional support for F-16 operations. Meanwhile, Moscow rejects a temporary Black Sea ceasefire while demanding Ukraine surrender Donbas. I consider how this military pressure intersects with Putin’s China meetings with Trump and Xi, Europe’s debate over direct diplomacy, and Russia’s continuing refusal to compromise.

snippet.title: Grupo de indígenas isolados sai da Amazônia e faz contato raro no Maranhão | O POVO NEWS
snippet.description:
